rules.selection: Choose the lowest priority number, then listed order, whose dependencies pass.
rules.mutation: Only passes and evidence may be changed by implementation iterations.
rules.completion: Every feature must pass before the later full-release .marathon/COMPLETE is created.
rules.marathon_scope: Marathon may implement only F001-F011, then must complete plan Gates G2-G4 and stop after BOOTSTRAP_HANDOFF reaches final.
rules.post_handoff_authority: After the pending handoff record, native bead state and generated release evidence are authoritative; this ledger is frozen audit input.

features.description: Native SQLite workspace initialization and versioned schema
acceptance: bead init creates a valid .beads workspace without touching unrelated files
Repeated initialization is safe and deterministic
Schema creation is transactional
evidence: cargo test --bin bead: 11 tests passed
cargo fmt --check: passed
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed

Idempotent initialization loads existing UUID from database

Foreign key constraints enforced with proper table ordering
WAL mode and busy-timeout configured correctly

features.description: Canonical native issue model with validated lifecycle and identifiers
acceptance: Model represents required and optional interchange data
Unknown extension fields can be retained
Invalid lifecycle transitions and malformed identifiers are rejected
evidence: cargo test --bin bead: 22 tests passed (11 new model tests)
cargo fmt --check: passed
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed
Implemented Issue struct with all required fields: id, title, priority, base_status, created_at, updated_at
Implemented all optional fields: description, notes, assignee, issue_type, manual_blocked, closed_at, close_reason, source_repo, profile, schema_ref, data
Implemented extensions HashMap with #[serde(flatten)] for unknown field preservation
Implemented validate_issue_id(): rejects empty, control chars, whitespace, path separators, NUL, >255 bytes
Implemented validate_title(): requires 1-4096 bytes
Implemented validate_priority(): enforces 0-4 range
Implemented validate_status_transition(): enforces plan section 3.3 transition matrix
Implemented BaseStatus enum with parse() for status string conversion
Implemented Issue::validate(): enforces closed state invariants and field rules
Implemented Issue::is_ready(): checks ready frontier predicate (open, unassigned, unblocked)
F002 acceptance criteria met: model represents interchange data, retains unknown fields, rejects invalid transitions

features.description: Create, list, and show commands with stable JSON output
acceptance: Create commits a new issue and prints only its ID on success
Create defaults an omitted description to empty
List supports JSON, status, assignee, exact ready-frontier filtering, comment projection, and explicit limit
Show returns the requested issue in NEEDLE-compatible JSON with none, unresolved, or all comment projection

features.description: Atomic server-selected claim and release behavior
acceptance: Selection and assignment occur in one write transaction
No eligible work is a successful structured domain result
Twenty simultaneous claimers never receive duplicate successful IDs

features.description: Update, close, and reopen lifecycle commands
acceptance: Status, assignee, and notes updates are atomic
release atomically transitions in-progress work to open and unassigned with the documented idempotency, conflict, output, and audit behavior
clear-assignee handles only open assigned work and generic update cannot bypass reopen for a closed bead
Close, reopen, and release satisfy the complete operation-by-base-state idempotency/conflict matrix without duplicate timestamps or events
Close retains a required reason
Reopen restores the documented open lifecycle state
Label add and remove are idempotent
Dependency direction follows blocked, blocker, kind
Readiness changes atomically with blocker lifecycle
sync --flush-only observes one committed snapshot
Records and semantically unordered collections are stably ordered
The pre-F017 issues.jsonl destination replacement and checkpoint-state update are crash-safe and atomic

features.description: Validated JSONL import with unknown-field preservation
acceptance: Malformed input reports its line and activates no partial state
Unknown fields survive a same-profile round trip
Import accepts exactly one explicit input path and never discovers or ranks sibling roots heuristically
Pre-F017 sync import accepts only an empty initialized target and transactionally activates one fully validated issue-only checkpoint
Successful pre-F017 activation appends exactly one checkpoint-imported event and leaves checkpoint covered/live sequences equal and clean
Import dry-run performs full validation and reconciliation analysis with canonical counts while leaving every durable workspace byte unchanged
doctor performs read-only integrity checks
Pre-F017 doctor validates issues.jsonl against migration-1 checkpoint state while post-F017 doctor selects pointer-based checks by store layout
doctor --repair changes only diagnosed conditions through the applicable normal flush or compatibility-view reconstruction path
Warnings and repairs use the required stable prefixes
Capabilities identify contract and store-layout versions
Atomic claim, lifecycle, checkpoint, and command support are explicit
Priority capabilities describe P4 as claimable under fifo-v1 without post-0.1 opt-in semantics
The commands inventory exactly matches every application-defined visible public root command
Schema catalog entries distinguish validation support from concrete lossless consume and emit operation paths
Unsupported profiles fail closed

features.description: Complete NEEDLE v1 subprocess compatibility suite
acceptance: Every required command is exercised as a subprocess
HOME and workspace are isolated for every subprocess test
stdout, stderr, exit status, and filesystem effects satisfy the contract

features.description: Interchange profiles for br-v1 and bf-v1
acceptance: Profiles are explicit and versioned
Every lossy transformation is reported
Fixtures are independently authored or sanitized black-box observations
Migration never overwrites its input
Source and target profiles are explicit and every input, output, and optional receipt path is distinct and non-overwriting
Dry-run validates without activating destination state
Stdout and any requested receipt file carry the canonical receipt/report with hashes, transformation counts, and deterministic preview semantics

features.description: Rapid-fire lifecycle stress and capacity benchmark harness
acceptance: Deterministic workloads cover claim-close, claim-release, mixed lifecycle, and dependency churn without duplicate claims or final-state divergence
Fast verification covers 100 and 1000 beads while the full driver reports every scale from 100 through 1000000 beads

Agent saturation sweeps cover 1 through 200 agents at approximately logarithmic steps across independent, chain, wide-DAG, diamond, and mixed-lifecycle datasets and report frontier, latency, throughput, SQLite contention/write amplification, cache, resources, and highest-supported-agent results
Uncompleted large-scale runs report an explicit resource-limited result instead of silently skipping a scale

features.description: Complete CLI help tree and generated section-1 man pages
acceptance: Every public command, subcommand, argument, option, value domain, default, conflict, and requirement has tested short and long help
bead --help, every nested --help path, and equivalent bead help paths work without workspace access or mutation
Root help and bead(1) explain the intended workflow, ready frontier, lifecycle transitions, blocking semantics, atomic claim, and live-SQLite versus flushed-JSONL boundary
Reproducible bead(1) and per-command section-1 man pages are generated from the authoritative command tree with required reference sections and valid cross-links
Help/man drift tests pass and every expected page plus explicit installation guidance is included in the packaged crate

features.description: Adaptive Git-trackable sharded checkpoints with forensic history
features.spec: research/specs/checkpoint-set-v1.md (required and not yet present; plan prose is nonnormative)
acceptance: Every flush captures all lifecycle states, complete portable bead content, dependencies, comments, structured extensions, and the continuous durable audit-event history
An independently reviewed normative checkpoint-set-v1 specification and conformance fixtures exist before implementation begins
Native monoliths use typed issue, event, and provenance-receipt records and represent issue-less workspace events without duplication or synthetic issues

Native checkpoints use an authoritative atomic current-generation pointer and deterministically switch from one forensic JSONL monolith to a manifest-backed content-addressed prefix-sharded issue and sequence-sharded event corpus while issues.jsonl remains issue-only interchange

Every pointer-selected root is immutable and content-addressed; shard splits rewrite only the overflowing prefix, sealed event shards remain immutable, and pointer/tombstone mode transitions preserve an authoritative verified root across interruption

Explicit empty-store restore and provenance-preserving merge validate UUIDs, event identities and continuity, hashes, partitions, counts, uniqueness, replayed state, and graph semantics before activation
Durable restore and merge receipts round-trip through monolithic and sharded checkpoints while dry-run and failed-operation material remain nondurable
Checkpoint artifacts are not ignored, sync reports changed Git-trackable paths, and documentation requires an external flush-before-commit workflow without bead-rs invoking Git
Final capabilities enumerate every normative forensic checkpoint format, mode, and readable/writable public schema introduced by checkpoint-set-v1

features.description: Release packaging, installation, and license verification
acceptance: cargo package succeeds from a clean checkout
Packaged installation provides the bead executable
Apache-2.0 license, NOTICE, README, and provenance ship in the package
